sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: A Go engineer who can only write code but cannot ship it reliably is incomplete. CI/CD questions test your understanding of the full delivery pipeline—from a git push to a running Kubernetes pod. Go's fast compile times and small binaries make CI pipelines very efficient, but you still need to understand module caching, lint gates, race detection in CI, and zero-downtime deployment strategies.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body: A Go CI pipeline has four gates that must all pass before a merge: (1) Lint: golangci-lint with staticcheck, errcheck, govet. (2) Test: go test -race -count=1 ./... with coverage threshold. (3) Build: go build produces the binary; docker build tags the image. (4) Deploy: push image to registry, apply Kubernetes manifests or trigger ArgoCD sync. Cache go module downloads and build cache between runs to keep pipeline under 3 minutes for a typical service.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body: 1. GitHub Actions for Go: actions/setup-go with go-version-file: go.mod, cache: true for module download cache. 2. go test in CI: -race, -coverprofile=coverage.out, go tool cover -func to enforce a minimum coverage %. 3. golangci-lint: .golangci.yml configuration, enabled linters (staticcheck, errcheck, gocritic, revive), --fix for auto-fixable issues. 4. Go binary caching: actions/cache on key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}, cache GOPATH/pkg/mod and ~/.cache/go-build. 5. Deployment patterns: blue-green (two identical environments), canary (gradual traffic shift), rolling update (Kubernetes default). 6. Kubernetes deployment: Deployment manifest, readinessProbe, livenessProbe, resource requests/limits, HPA for Go services.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body: • 'Walk me through your Go CI pipeline.' → lint gate, race-detected tests, coverage check, Docker build, push to registry, deploy. • 'How do you speed up a Go CI pipeline?' → cache go module downloads and build cache, parallelise lint and test jobs, use multi-stage Docker build layer caching. • 'What linters do you run on Go code and why?' → golangci-lint with staticcheck (correctness), errcheck (unchecked errors), govet (suspicious constructs), goimports (formatting). • 'How do you do a zero-downtime deployment of a Go service on Kubernetes?' → rolling update with maxUnavailable: 0, readinessProbe to gate traffic, graceful shutdown with context cancellation.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: "My Go CI pipeline in GitHub Actions has three jobs that run in parallel after a lint gate: test, build-image, and security-scan. The lint job runs golangci-lint with staticcheck and errcheck enabled—any unchecked error is a pipeline failure. The test job runs go test -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...; I fail the build if coverage drops below 80%. Build caching uses actions/cache keyed on go.sum so module downloads are skipped on repeat runs. The Docker build job uses BuildKit with layer caching pushed to the registry. Deployment to Kubernetes is a rolling update with maxUnavailable: 0 and a readinessProbe on /healthz so no traffic reaches a pod until it is ready. I use ArgoCD for GitOps so the deploy job just pushes the new image tag to the Helm values file."
